sanskrit: śṛṇu rāma mahābāho yadartham aham āhataḥ pitāmahena devena preṣito 'smi mahābala
english: Listen, O Rāma, mighty-armed one, great in strength — for what purpose I have been commissioned and sent here by the god Pitāmaha.

sanskrit: tavāhaṃ pūrvake bhāve putraḥ parapuraṃjaya māyāsaṃbhāvito vīra kālaḥ sarvasamāharaḥ
english: I am your son from your prior existence, O conqueror of enemy cities; O hero, brought forth through māyā — I am Kāla, the all-consumer.

sanskrit: pitāmahaś ca bhagavān āha lokapatiḥ prabhuḥ samayas te mahābāho svarlokān parirakṣitum
english: And the blessed Pitāmaha, lord of worlds and sovereign, said: 'The time has come for you, O mighty-armed one, to protect the celestial realms.'

sanskrit: saṃkṣipya ca purā lokān māyayā svayam eva hi mahārṇave śayāno 'psu māṃ tvaṃ pūrvam ajījanaḥ
english: Having once contracted the worlds through māyā yourself, lying upon the great ocean on the waters, you formerly brought me forth.

sanskrit: bhogavantaṃ tato nāgam anantam udake śayam māyayā janayitvā tvaṃ dvau ca sattvau mahābalau
english: Then, having created through māyā Ananta, the mighty serpent lying in the water, and also two mighty beings —

sanskrit: madhuṃ ca kaiṭabhaṃ caiva yayor asthicayair vṛtā iyaṃ parvatasaṃbādhā medinī cābhavan mahī
english: — Madhu and Kaiṭabha, by whose heaped bones this earth, crowded with mountains, came to be formed —

sanskrit: padme divyārkasaṃkāśe nābhyām utpādya mām api prājāpatyaṃ tvayā karma sarvaṃ mayi niveśitam
english: — producing me from your navel upon the divine lotus blazing like the sun, you entrusted to me all the creative work of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ saṃnyastabhāro hi tvām upāse jagatpatim rakṣāṃ vidhatsva bhūteṣu mama tejaḥ karo bhavān
english: Thus I, having laid down my burden, worship you, lord of the universe; grant protection to beings — you are the source of my splendor.

sanskrit: tatas tvam api durdharṣas tasmād bhāvāt sanātanāt rakṣārthaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viṣṇutvam upajagmivān
english: And you, the invincible one, from that eternal state assumed the nature of Viṣṇu for the protection of all beings.

sanskrit: adityāṃ vīryavān putro bhrātṝṇāṃ harṣavardhanaḥ samutpanneṣu kṛtyeṣu lokasāhyāya kalpase
english: Born of Aditi as a mighty son, you who increase the joy of your brothers — whenever deeds arise, you stand ready to aid the world.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ vitrāsyamānāsu prajāsu jagatāṃ vara rāvaṇasya vadhākāṅkṣī mānuṣeṣu mano 'dadhāḥ
english: You, the best of the worlds, with your subjects in terror, desiring the slaying of Rāvaṇa, turned your mind toward birth among humans.

sanskrit: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca kṛtvā vāsasya niyatiṃ svayam evātmanaḥ purā
english: You yourself ordained for yourself, of old, the measure of your sojourn — ten thousand years and ten hundred years.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ manomayaḥ putraḥ pūrṇāyur mānuṣeṣv iha kālo naravaraśreṣṭha samīpam upavartitum
english: You, whose son is mind-born, having fulfilled your allotted lifespan among men here — the time has come to approach, O best of best men.

sanskrit: yadi bhūyo mahārāja prajā icchasy upāsitum vasa vā vīra bhadraṃ te evam āha pitāmahaḥ
english: If, O great king, you wish to tend your subjects yet longer, then dwell on — O hero, may it be well with you; thus spoke Pitāmaha.

sanskrit: atha vā vijigīṣā te suralokāya rāghava sanāthā viṣṇunā devā bhavantu vigatajvarāḥ
english: Or if you have the desire to conquer the realm of the gods, O Rāghava, let the gods be protected by Viṣṇu and freed from affliction.

sanskrit: śrutvā pitāmahenoktaṃ vākyaṃ kālasamīritam rāghavaḥ prahasan vākyaṃ sarvasaṃhāram abravīt
english: Having heard the words spoken by Pitāmaha and conveyed by Kāla, Rāghava, smiling, spoke to Kāla, the all-withdrawer.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ me devadevasya vākyaṃ paramam adbhutam prītir hi mahatī jātā tavāgamanasaṃbhavā
english: "I have heard the supremely wondrous words of the god of gods; great delight has arisen in me from your coming."

sanskrit: bhadraṃ te 'stu gamiṣyāmi yata evāham āgataḥ hṛd gato hy asi saṃprāpto na me 'sty atra vicāraṇā
english: "May it be well with you. I shall go to that very place whence I have come — for you have truly entered my heart now that you have arrived; I have no hesitation in this."

sanskrit: mayā hi sarvakṛtyeṣu devānāṃ vaśavartinām sthātavyaṃ sarvasaṃhāre yathā hy āha pitāmahaḥ
english: "For in all the affairs of the gods who are subject to me, I must stand firm at the final withdrawal of all — just as Pitāmaha has declared."

sanskrit: tathā tayoḥ kathayator durvāsā bhagavān ṛṣiḥ rāmasya darśanākāṅkṣī rājadvāram upāgamat
english: While those two were thus conversing, the blessed sage Durvāsas, desirous of an audience with Rāma, approached the gate of the palace.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya ca saumitrim uvāca ṛṣisattamaḥ rāmaṃ darśaya me śīghraṃ purā me 'rtho 'tivartate
english: Approaching Saumitri, that foremost of sages said: "Show me Rāma at once — my purpose will lapse if delayed."

sanskrit: munes tu bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā abhivādya mahātmānaṃ vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Hearing the sage's words, Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, saluted the great-souled one and spoke these words.

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryaṃ brūhi bhagavan ko vārthaḥ kiṃ karomy aham vyagro hi rāghavo brahman muhūrtaṃ vā pratīkṣatām
english: "Tell me, revered one, what is the matter — what is the purpose, what should I do? Rāghava is occupied, O brahmin; please wait but a moment."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā ṛṣiśārdūlaḥ krodhena kaluṣīkṛtaḥ uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyaṃ nirdahann iva cakṣuṣā
english: Hearing this, that tiger among sages, inflamed with anger, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa with words that seemed to burn him with a glance.

sanskrit: asmin kṣaṇe māṃ saumitre rāmāya prativedaya viṣayaṃ tvāṃ puraṃ caiva śapiṣye rāghavaṃ tathā
english: "This very instant, O Saumitri, announce me to Rāma — otherwise I shall curse you, your realm, your city, and Rāghava as well."

sanskrit: bharataṃ caiva saumitre yuṣmākaṃ yā ca saṃtatiḥ na hi śakṣyāmy ahaṃ bhūyo manyuṃ dhārayituṃ hṛdi
english: "And Bharata, O Saumitri, and all your posterity — for I am no longer able to hold back my anger in my heart."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā ghorasaṃkāśaṃ vākyaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ cintayām āsa manasā tasya vākyasya niścayam
english: Hearing those fearsome-seeming words of that great-souled one, Lakṣmaṇa reflected in his mind on the import of those words.

sanskrit: ekasya maraṇaṃ me 'stu mā bhūt sarvavināśanam iti buddhyā viniścitya rāghavāya nyavedayat
english: "Let death be mine alone; let there be no destruction of all" — having resolved this in his understanding, he announced it to Rāghava.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaḥ kālaṃ visṛjya ca niṣpatya tvaritaṃ rājā atreḥ putraṃ dadarśa ha
english: Hearing Lakṣmaṇa's words, Rāma dismissed Kāla and, stepping out swiftly, the king beheld the son of Atri.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā kiṃ kāryam iti kākutsthaḥ kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata
english: Bowing to that great-souled one blazing as it were with splendor, Kākutstha, with hands folded in reverence, asked: "What is the purpose?"

sanskrit: tad vākyaṃ rāghaveṇṇoktaṃ śrutvā munivaraḥ prabhuḥ pratyāha rāmaṃ durvāsāḥ śrūyatāṃ dharmavatsala
english: Hearing those words spoken by Rāghava, the great sage and lord Durvāsas replied to Rāma: "Hear me, O you who cherish righteousness."

sanskrit: adya varṣasahasrasya samāptir mama rāghava so 'haṃ bhojanam icchāmi yathāsiddhaṃ tavānagha
english: "Today marks the completion of my thousand-year vow, O Rāghava; I, O sinless one, desire food — whatever is prepared in your household."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ rāmo harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ bhojanaṃ munimukhyāya yathāsiddham upāharat
english: Hearing those words, Rāma, filled with great delight, offered to the foremost of sages the food that had been prepared.

sanskrit: sa tu bhuktvā muniśreṣṭhas tad annam amṛtopamam sādhu rāmeti saṃbhāṣya svam āśramam upāgamat
english: That best of sages, having eaten that food comparable to nectar, addressed Rāma with "Well done, Rāma" and returned to his own hermitage.

sanskrit: tasmin gate mahātejā rāghavaḥ prītamānasaḥ saṃsmṛtya kālavākyāni tato duḥkham upeyivān
english: When he had departed, the greatly resplendent Rāghava, whose mind had been glad, recalled the words of Kāla and was then overcome with sorrow.

sanskrit: duḥkhena ca susaṃtaptaḥ smṛtvā tad ghoradarśanam avānmukho dīnamanā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha
english: Deeply tormented by grief, recalling that terrible encounter, he stood with downcast face, dejected in mind, unable to speak.

sanskrit: tato buddhyā viniścitya kālavākyāni rāghavaḥ naitad astīti coktvā sa tūṣṇīm āsīn mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then Rāghava of great renown, having resolved in his mind the words of Kāla, said only "This is not to be" — and sat in silence.

sanskrit: avāṅmukham atho dīnaṃ dṛṣṭvā somam ivāplutam rāghavaṃ lakṣmaṇo vākyaṃ hṛṣṭo madhuram abravīt
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, seeing Rāghava downcast and wretched like the moon overcome by eclipse, joyfully spoke sweet words.

sanskrit: na saṃtāpaṃ mahābāho madarthaṃ kartum arhasi pūrvanirmāṇabaddhā hi kālasya gatir īdṛśī
english: "You ought not to grieve on my account, O mighty-armed one — for such is the course of Kāla, bound by the ordinance laid down of old."

sanskrit: jahi māṃ saumya visrabdaḥ pratijñāṃ paripālaya hīnapratijñāḥ kākutstha prayānti narakaṃ narāḥ
english: "Slay me, O gentle one, without hesitation, and uphold your vow — for men who fail in their vows descend to hell, O Kākutstha."

sanskrit: yadi prītir mahārāja yady anugrāhyatā mayi jahi māṃ nirviśaṅkas tvaṃ dharmaṃ vardhaya rāghava
english: "If there is love in you, O great king, if I am worthy of your favor — slay me without hesitation, O Rāghava, and let righteousness flourish."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena tathoktas tu rāmaḥ pracalitendriyaḥ mantriṇaḥ samupānīya tathaiva ca purodhasaṃ
english: Thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma, with agitated senses, summoned his ministers and likewise the chief priest.

sanskrit: abravīc ca yathāvṛttaṃ teṣāṃ madhye narādhipaḥ durvāso'bhigamaṃ caiva pratijñāṃ tāpasasya ca
english: And the lord of men recounted to them, in their midst, all that had happened — both the arrival of Durvāsas and the vow that had been made with the ascetic.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā mantriṇaḥ sarve sopādhyāyāḥ samāsata vasiṣṭhas tu mahātejā vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Hearing this, all the ministers together with the preceptors sat in assembly; then Vasiṣṭha of great splendor spoke these words.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭam etan mahābāho kṣayaṃ te lomaharṣaṇam lakṣmaṇena viyogaś ca tava rāma mahāyaśaḥ
english: "This has been foreseen, O mighty-armed Rāma of great renown — your end, which causes the hair to stand on end, and your separation from Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tyajainaṃ balavān kālo mā pratijñāṃ vṛthā kṛthāḥ vinaṣṭāyāṃ pratijñāyāṃ dharmo hi vilayaṃ vrajet
english: "Abandon him — Kāla is powerful; do not render your vow futile, for when a vow is destroyed, righteousness goes to ruin."

sanskrit: tato dharme vinaṣṭe tu trailokye sacarācaram sadevarṣigaṇaṃ sarvaṃ vinaśyeta na saṃśayaḥ
english: "And when righteousness is destroyed, all that is movable and immovable in the three worlds, together with the hosts of gods and sages, would perish — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla trailokyasyābhipālanam lakṣmaṇasya vadhenādya jagat svasthaṃ kuruṣva ha
english: "Therefore you, tiger among men, who are the protector of the three worlds — render the world whole today by the death of Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tat samavetānāṃ vākyaṃ dharmārthasaṃhitam śrutvā pariṣado madhye rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Hearing that counsel of those assembled — fraught with righteousness and purpose — Rāma, in the midst of the assembly, addressed Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: visarjaye tvāṃ saumitre mā bhūd dharmaviparyayaḥ tyāgo vadho vā vihitaḥ sādhūnām ubhayaṃ samam
english: "I release you, O Saumitri — let there be no inversion of righteousness; for the righteous, renunciation and death are equally ordained, and both are the same."

sanskrit: rāmeṇa bhāṣite vākye bāṣpavyākulitekṣaṇaḥ lakṣmaṇas tvaritaḥ prāyāt svagṛhaṃ na viveśa ha
english: When Rāma had spoken those words, Lakṣmaṇa, his eyes blurred with tears, departed in haste — but he did not enter his house.

sanskrit: sa gatvā sarayūtīram upaspṛśya kṛtāñjaliḥ nigṛhya sarvasrotāṃsi niḥśvāsaṃ na mumoca ha
english: He went to the bank of the Sarayū, sipped its waters, and with hands folded in reverence, restrained all his vital channels and breathed not a breath.

sanskrit: anucchvasantaṃ yuktaṃ taṃ saśakrāḥ sāpsarogaṇāḥ devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ sarve puṣpair avakiraṃs tadā
english: As he stood thus absorbed, not breathing — all the gods together with Śakra and the troops of apsarasas, together with the hosts of sages, showered him with flowers.

sanskrit: adṛśyaṃ sarvam anujaiḥ saśarīraṃ mahābalam pragṛhya lakṣmaṇaṃ śakro divaṃ saṃpraviveśa ha
english: As he became invisible to all his younger brothers, Śakra took up Lakṣmaṇa — mighty in strength and still in his body — and entered heaven.

sanskrit: tato viṣṇoś caturbhāgam āgataṃ surasattamāḥ hṛṣṭāḥ pramuditāḥ sarve 'pūjayan ṛṣibhiḥ saha
english: Then the best of gods, all rejoicing and delighted, together with the sages, honored the fourth part of Viṣṇu that had returned.
